name: Hubble Space Telescope (STS-31)
payload: Hubble Space Telescope: 43.5 ft (13.3 m) long, about 11,000 kg, 94.5 in (2.4 m) main mirror; crew of five
first: The Shuttle flight that lifted the Hubble Space Telescope out of Discovery's payload bay and released it from the robotic arm
description: STS-31 carried the Hubble Space Telescope into a 332 by 331 nautical mile orbit and released it from Discovery's robotic arm. Discovery lifted off from Launch Complex 39B on 24 April 1990 at 12:33:51 UTC, two weeks after a first attempt was stopped by an auxiliary power unit. On 25 April, once panel 2 of the solar array had deployed on its third attempt, the arm released the telescope at 19:37:51 UTC; Bruce McCandless and Kathryn Sullivan, ready for a contingency spacewalk, were not needed. Discovery landed at Edwards Air Force Base on 29 April, after about 5 days in flight. Hubble is still in operation. Five Shuttle servicing missions between 1993 and 2009 repaired and upgraded it, the last in May 2009.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Discovery from Launch Complex 39B, 24 April 1990, 12:33:51 UTC; a first attempt on 10 April was stopped by an auxiliary power unit.

events.label: CIRCULARIZATION
events.note: A 33.5 ft/s thruster firing at 19:43:05 UTC put Discovery in a 332 by 331 nautical mile orbit (about 615 by 613 km).

events.label: ARRAY PANEL 2 STUCK
events.note: Panel 2 of the solar array failed to deploy on the first attempt, deployed partly on the second and fully on the third; the report gives no times.

events.label: HUBBLE RELEASED
events.note: Released from the arm at 19:37:51 UTC on 25 April; the contingency spacewalk was cancelled.

events.label: LANDING
events.note: Edwards Air Force Base, concrete runway 22, 29 April 1990, main gear down at 13:49:56 UTC.
